title: Auctions point to more price falls
full_text:
Auction clearances fell in Sydney and Melbourne after a week in which the Reserve Bank poured cold water on hopes for lower interest rates, pointing to further price declines in the east coast-dominated national market.
The combined capital city clearance rate lifted to 56.5 per cent last week - up from a preliminary 55.1 per cent - on the strength of smaller markets in Brisbane, Adelaide and Perth, but the two largest cities both softened after a stronger performance the previous week.
Higher rates, persistently high inflation and the fastest decline in investor borrowing in 3 years are hitting prices as vendors lower their expectations and as buyers - sensing more declines to come - hold back and wait for the market to soften further.
RBA governor Michele Bullock last week warned housing values have further to fall, even as she made it clear another rate rise remains an option for the central bank.
Tim Lawless, research director for data provider Cotality, said on Sunday that the trend for home values was "continuing to lose steam through August".
"At this level, the low auction success rate is still indicative of a market where values are falling, and buyers remain in the driver's seat. Clearance rates remain well below the decade average of 68 per cent."
Melbourne weakened the most as the city's preliminary clearance rate fell to 57.4, its lowest in three weeks, from 60.8 per cent, Cotality data showed.
In inner-eastern Malvern, a three-bedroom family home at 38 Johnstone Street passed in on a vendor bid of $2 million, but sold afterwards within the guide range of $2 million to $2.1 million, Jellis Craig sales agent Carla Fetter said. "It is a very patchy market and there's no rhyme or reason at the moment," Fetter said.
In Sydney, where the preliminary clearance rate slipped to 55.6 per cent from 57 per cent, a downsizing couple sold their three-bedroom family house in upper north shore Roseville for $2.33 million in an auction that started bidding at its guided price of $2.2 million.
In a falling market it made sense to sell quickly by auction, said vendor Peter, who asked not to disclose his surname. "We'd already bought our apartment and we just wanted to sell," he said.
In Brisbane, the preliminary clearance rate jumped to 51.9 per cent from 38.1 per cent in a market with 145 scheduled auctions. Buyers in the Queensland capital - particularly downsizing Baby Boomers with housing equity - are willing to spend money on luxury homes.
In South Brisbane, developer Mosaic sold a four-bedroom, 394-square-metre apartment in its 213-unit Riversdale development for $11 million, or an internal rate of $30,640 per square metre. This lifted sales revenue in the 39-level project at 91 Montague Road to $450 million out of a total $750 million.
"This transaction reflects the growing appeal of South Brisbane among prestige buyers," said Mosaic director Brook Monahan.
Adelaide's preliminary clearance rate jumped to 61.9 per cent from 46.8 per cent, with 88 scheduled auctions. In Canberra, the initial rate picked up to 60 per cent from 45.9 per cent a week earlier.
In Canberra's southern Woden district, a four-bedroom family home at 9 Cornelian Place sold under the hammer for $1.38 million, just over the $1.35 million reserve, to a young family renting in the area.
The property was marketed by The Agency's Stu Hamill.
